goal: Stops other code from arbitrarily setting an HTTPRequest's internal parsing state, closing off a class of bugs where state could be set inconsistently.
Also flattens the HTTP request-reading code path into fewer, clearer methods.
reviewability: Ready. Discussion has settled into nits, and the author has kept the PR updated through multiple rounds of comments and splits.
agreement: Strong support because two reviewers gave concept ACKs and one gave a tested ACK on the final commit (jeanpablojp, winterrdog, janb84).
All raised nits were addressed by the author in subsequent pushes, no standing objections remain.

result.summary: This PR removes HTTPRequest::SetState(), which let any code with a reference to an HTTPRequest directly mutate its internal parsing state enum, and replaces the three public LoadControlData/LoadHeaders/LoadBody methods with a single internal Load() method that returns the current state. It also extracts and then flattens HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequestInternal() out of the previously static TryReadRequest()/ReadRequest() pair, tightening encapsulation around the client's receive buffer handling. Tests and the fuzz harness are updated to use the new Load()-based API.
result.problem: After #35829 made HTTPRequest fields private, the state enum could still be externally mutated via SetState(), undermining the encapsulation that PR intended and leaving room for future bugs where code sets an inconsistent state. This affects maintainers of the HTTP server who rely on the state machine's invariants being enforced by the type system rather than convention.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Modifies src/httpserver.cpp and src/httpserver.h, the HTTP server that carries JSON-RPC, tightening encapsulation of the request state machine used by every RPC call.
categories.rationale: This is an internal encapsulation improvement to the HTTP server's request-parsing state machine, not a behavior or correctness fix visible to RPC callers. janb84 called it 'a better design' because it makes an existing convention compiler-enforced, reducing risk of future misuse, but no bug or user-facing gap motivates it. It has some leverage for other in-flight HTTP server refactors (#36159, #36204) but is otherwise a maintainability improvement within RPC's transport layer.

result.card: This PR removes HTTPRequest::SetState(), closing a gap where any code holding a request reference could arbitrarily mutate its internal parsing state, and consolidates the three public Load* methods into a single private Load() call, also flattening the client's read-request path. The problem is one of encapsulation and design hygiene in the HTTP server that carries RPC traffic, not a user-visible bug; janb84 called it 'a better design' since it makes the no-arbitrary-state rule compiler-enforced. Review is complete: three reviewers gave concept ACKs, one gave a tested ACK, and all nits raised were addressed across many force-pushes with no open objections. It conflicts with three other open PRs touching the same files (#36204, #36160, #36135), so sequencing matters, but the PR itself is Ready for merge consideration. Priority is modest since the benefit is internal robustness rather than a fix to a felt bug or feature gap.
